title: "I'd rather go to jail than getting beat up by my dad" Kaden (15)
summary: Jordan interviews 15-year-old Kaden, who disclosed that his father was physically abusing him by punching him in the head. Kaden also reported that he believed his father drugged him and his girlfriend and sexually assaulted his girlfriend while Kaden was blacked out. Kaden had also reported to the CSW that his father would threaten him sexually. Jordan anticipated Kaden might be reluctant to discuss the sexual threats given prior reports that he couldn't remember if any sexual abuse occurred.

title: "I can tell it was bleeding cause I like tasted blood" Ellie (9)
summary: Cara interviews 9-year-old Ellie, who disclosed to a school counselor that her mother hits her in the mouth and eye with an open hand. The most recent incident occurred the night before because Ellie didn't go to sleep on time. School officials reported that the mother treats Ellie and her older brother differently — punishing Ellie by restricting school activities and not providing equal resources. The team anticipated Ellie might minimize the abuse during the interview, as she had begun to do so with the CSW.

title: "They keep on asking questions even though I tell them everything that's the truth" Kaylee (11)
summary: Jordan interviews 11-year-old Kaylee, who disclosed self-harm in response to ongoing conflict between her brother and mother. Her brother gets violent and punches holes in the walls. Given Kaylee's disclosed prior suicide attempt, Jordan knew she might need to conduct a suicide assessment. During the interview, Kaylee became upset and combative about being interviewed repeatedly by multiple professionals about the same allegations, requiring Jordan to explain the purpose of the interview.

title: "My dad said it was not my dad, it was a person I was dreaming" Morgan (9)
summary: Chrissy interviews 9-year-old Morgan (conducted in 2017), who disclosed that her father would wake her up to do 'sexy stuff,' including touching her butt with his 'front part' until 'white stuff' came out. Prior to the interview, it was discovered that Morgan's mother and father had reunited. During the interview, Morgan recanted her allegations, claiming it was just a dream and that she had been caught watching a 'sexy movie.'

title: The First Jane Doe in the Epstein case: S.G. (14)
summary: This webinar reviews the police interview with S.G. and her grand jury testimony — S.G. was the first child victim interviewed in the Palm Beach Epstein investigation. S.G. initially denied everything, but gradually disclosed increasingly serious abuse over the course of the interviews.

title: "Stuck in the same cycle everyday" Ashley (14)
summary: Jordan interviews 14-year-old Ashley, who disclosed that her stepfather began touching her under the guise of play wrestling, with multiple incidents of stepfather explicitly asking her to let him touch her. Prior to the interview, Ashley and her mother were AWOL from DCFS, so Jordan anticipated Ashley might be reluctant to disclose.

title: "Everyone's giving me different words for it" Claire (17)
summary: Jordan interviews 17-year-old Claire, who disclosed that her father had been forcing her to have sex with him for two years, occurring every other night while the rest of the family slept. Because Claire described the details of the different incidents as identical, Jordan had to use creative techniques to elicit information about multiple episodes.

title: "All I ever feel is guilt, and it's exhausting" Josie (15)
summary: Cara interviews 15-year-old Josie, who disclosed that her stepfather had been sexually abusing her since she was four years old. In prior interviews with police and social workers, Josie reported difficulty remembering details because she had tried to forget. Josie's discussion of self-blame and feeling like an active participant led Cara to adjust her questioning techniques during the interview.

title: "Gave me the ick" Back to Basics: Ruth (11)
summary: Jordan interviews 11-year-old Ruth, who disclosed that her stepfather was touching her inappropriately under the ruse of tickling, and that he would take pictures of her in the shower. Ruth initially denied these allegations to her social worker, but later re-disclosed to the police. Jordan anticipated reluctance going into the interview.

title: "With a stick and a shoe and a hanger" Skylar (7)
summary: Jordan interviews 7-year-old Skylar, whose older sister Callie (12) had disclosed severe sexual abuse by their stepfather. Skylar was initially taken for a forensic interview at another center where she denied witnessing or experiencing abuse. A month later, she disclosed to her caregiver that her father had touched her everywhere and told her to keep quiet.

title: Back to Basics: Reviewing the Ten Step Interview Brynne (12)
summary: Cara interviews 12-year-old Brynne, who disclosed that her father tried to forcefully remove her from school and had touched her and made her feel uncomfortable. Brynne reported being scared of her father because she witnessed him physically assault her adult sister, and that her father would insist she change her clothes out in the open. During the interview, Brynne discusses the sexual intent behind the touch, asking, 'if he did that, what if he thought about doing other things to me?'

title: "Like, no matter what, he's my dad." Bella (17)
summary: Jordan interviews 17-year-old Bella, who disclosed that her tattoo artist had sexually assaulted her. When asked why she hadn't told her mother, Bella revealed that her own father had sexually assaulted her when she was 5 years old, and she thought it was normal because he was her father. After her initial disclosure, Bella partially recanted by telling professionals that it was her cousin who had sexually assaulted her.

title: "They want to catch if I'm lying or not" Caroline (14)
summary: Cara interviews 14-year-old Caroline, who disclosed that after her stepfather came home drunk, he cornered her in the kitchen and sexually assaulted her, telling her she was 'beautiful and hot.' Caroline reported feeling uncomfortable and weird, and later recalled additional abuse after her initial disclosure.

title: "I don't know" Bethany (5)
summary: Jordan interviews 5-year-old Bethany, who disclosed that her 9-year-old sister Victoria had touched her. When their mother found out, she physically assaulted Victoria, leading to police being called. During the forensic interview, Bethany responded to most of Jordan's questions with 'I don't know.'

title: Disbelieving Witness Part II: Kayla (15) and Maria (16)
summary: Part II of the Kayla series — following up on Cara's interview with 15-year-old Kayla, who disclosed that her maternal uncle/adoptive father had been sexually touching her with force. Kayla described a specific incident where her cousin Maria was in the room. When Maria (16) was interviewed by Jordan, she denied ever witnessing her biological father abuse Kayla.

title: "He said, are you in love with me" Kayla (15)
summary: Cara interviews 15-year-old Kayla, who disclosed that her maternal uncle/adoptive father had been sexually touching her inappropriately. Kayla described forceful abuse and a specific incident where her cousin Maria was in the room. When Maria was later interviewed, she denied ever witnessing her biological father abuse Kayla.

title: "Stop. Just color." Isabela (4)
summary: Jordan interviews 4-year-old Isabela, who disclosed to a school teacher that her uncle was hurting her with his 'p.' She continued to disclose to other professionals, but struggled with consistency and memory due to her age.

title: "I wanted to be like taken away from my mom" Kira (10)
summary: Part 2 of a two-part series examining interviews of sisters Tammy (12) and Kira (10). Tammy disclosed that their uncle would touch both sisters at night in bed from kindergarten through second grade. Kira disclosed that her mother told both sisters to say that nothing happened.

title: "All the times it was just the same" Tammy (12)
summary: Part 1 of a two-part series examining interviews of sisters Tammy (12) and Kira (10). Tammy disclosed that their uncle would touch her and her sister Kira at night in bed from kindergarten to second grade. Kira disclosed that their mother told the sisters to say that nothing happened.

title: Interviewing an Older Teen: "People say that these days, teenagers tend to lie to get out of anything"
summary: Cara interviews 17-year-old Ashley, who disclosed that her father was physically and sexually abusive when she was told she would be moving in with him. Ashley described father forcibly removing her clothing. Both her adult sibling and the police believed Ashley was fabricating the allegations because she did not want to live with her father.

title: Sibling Witness Interview to Corroborate Abuse
summary: Jordan conducts a witness and screening interview with 7-year-old Johana, following her interview with Johana's older sister Rut (11) about sexual abuse allegations against their stepfather. In her interview, Rut described several instances where Johana could have witnessed the abuse. When Jordan interviewed Johana, even though Johana didn't believe Rut, the interview still provided useful information for the investigation.

title: Novice Interviewer vs Reluctant Child
summary: The team reviews an interview conducted in 2017 with 12-year-old Madison by one of their former forensic interviewers. Madison first disclosed sexual abuse from her father when re-enacting the abuse with her sister, and then reported experiencing repeated abuse.

title: Suicide and Self-Harm Disclosure During Forensic Interviews: How & When to Assess Risk & Safety Plan
summary: Jordan Sargent and Lauren Maltby (PhD) present a condensed version of their talk from the 40th Annual San Diego International Conference on Child and Family Maltreatment. The presentation covers best practices for assessing suicidality and self-harm mentioned during forensic interviews, how to positively pair open-ended invitations with closed-ended screening questions from standardized tools like the ASQ, how to respond to severe emotional reactions, and post-interview safety planning.

title: "If your dad was here, he could buy you anything" Ally (12)
summary: Cara interviews 12-year-old Ally, who disclosed to a doctor that someone in her home was touching her but would not say who. When interviewed by social workers, she disclosed it was her stepfather. The next day, Ally told her mother she had made it all up.

title: When the Defense Investigator Leads the Child
summary: The team reviews a homicide case involving 9-year-old Kylie, the only child witness to her mother's violent altercation with a homeless man who attempted to enter their vehicle. Kylie's mother then struck the victim with her car and fled the scene. After the mother was arrested, Kylie underwent both a forensic interview and a defense investigative interview conducted by the mother's defense attorney.

title: "It felt like it wasn't an accident"
summary: Gabrielle interviews 13-year-old Charlotte (Gabrielle's 3rd interview). Prior to a visitation with their father, Charlotte and her brother Diego told their mother that their father was touching them inappropriately. When interviewed by law enforcement, Charlotte asked the officer to tell her father to stop touching them on their private parts.

title: "I'm Scared": Kali (10) What to do when the child wants to stop
summary: Jordan interviews 10-year-old Kali, who had disclosed sexual abuse to police twice — first in Nevada and then months later in Los Angeles. Kali reported that her mother began sexually abusing her when she was 5 years old. Kali was extremely reluctant to disclose general and specific details, requiring multiple breaks as she would emotionally shut down when discussing body parts and specific acts.

title: "Okay, Porky" Interviewing the Sassy Teen
summary: Jordan interviews 14-year-old Katelynn, whose mother called the police on her during a family altercation. During the law enforcement interview, Katelynn disclosed that her father had sexually abused her when she was 5 years old. Katelynn has a history of suicidality, substance use, and running away.

title: "We never did like him" Back to Basics Interviewing Refresher
summary: Jordan reviews her 2019 interview with 11-year-old Isabella, who reported to a school counselor that her father had been sexually abusing her from ages 4 to 9. Isabella's stepfather was arrested and later convicted under California Penal Code 288.5(a) for Continuous Sexual Abuse of a Child.

title: Conflicting Sibling Testimony
summary: Part 2 of a two-part webinar reviewing Cara's forensic interviews of siblings Aliyah (10) and Malachi (9). Aliyah reported that her mother had multiple personalities, and her alternate personality 'Phoenix' would often lie on top of her in an ambiguous way. The team reviews Malachi's interview as a potential witness.

title: Double Recantation
summary: Jordan interviews two sisters, 13-year-old Keyla and 9-year-old Isabella, who alleged abuse by their stepfather. Keyla made allegations in two separate police interviews but later recanted and denied her first two forensic interviews. Isabella spontaneously reported feeling uncomfortable when stepfather was tickling her, but later said the incident was only a prank. Isabella was forthcoming about family events that helped explain Keyla's recantation.

title: Gabby's First Interview
summary: Gabrielle's first interview is reviewed, in which she interviewed 13-year-old Hadasha. Hadasha disclosed physical abuse from her mother and sexual abuse from her mother's boyfriend. Hadasha had previously disclosed abuse from mother's boyfriend in 2023, but those investigations were unfounded after she recanted.

title: Jorge (11)
summary: The team reviews an anonymized interview conducted by another center with Jorge, an 11-year-old trans boy who alleged abuse from his mother's boyfriend. While his initial disclosure described moderate abuse, in the interview Jorge disclosed repeated rape.

title: Brother-Brother Abuse: Body Cam VS Forensic Interview
summary: Part 2 of a two-part series reviewing a complicated case involving four brothers. The team examines 12-year-old Jante's forensic interview and police interview. Jante was the first brother to initially disclose, but minimized the abuse in his forensic interview.

title: Teen Disclosure of Brother-Brother Abuse
summary: Part 1 of a two-part series reviewing a case involving four brothers. Jordan interviews 14-year-old Jamari, whose brother reported witnessing Jamari being sexually abused by their 17-year-old brother. Jamari had denied the abuse when interviewed by social workers and law enforcement, but in Jordan's interview disclosed abuse for the first time while sharing feelings of embarrassment and reluctance.

title: Reluctance and Non-Response: When to Conduct a Follow-Up Interview
summary: The team reviews two interviews Tom and Jordan conducted with 11-year-old Adalyn, who disclosed severe abuse from her paternal grandfather. Adalyn was extremely reluctant and unable to even speak in her first interview. She agreed to return for a second interview with Jordan, where she disclosed some parts of the abuse before shutting down again.

title: Recantation Case Study
summary: Tom interviews 9-year-old Nasha, who initially disclosed sexual abuse from her mother's boyfriend and reported that her grandmother had allowed men to rape Nasha in exchange for money. The grandmother was arrested, but Nasha recanted the grandmother's abuse shortly after testifying at the preliminary hearing. The DA then invited Tom to interview Nasha.

title: Minimal Facts: Conflicts between Police and Forensic Interviewing
summary: The team reviews body cam footage from an interview Jordan conducted in September 2023 with 8-year-old Alondra, highlighting how challenges in police interviews can be avoided with more comprehensive minimal facts training for law enforcement.

title: Child Witness to Homicide Matthew (6): My dad is the best dad in the world
summary: The team reviews Tom's 2004 interview with 6-year-old Matthew, the only eyewitness to his mother's murder. Matthew recanted at trial, but the interview was admitted into evidence.

title: "I Don't Want to Explain It"
summary: Jordan's 2019 interview with 10-year-old Valerie, who disclosed that her father raped her on two occasions in the same day.

title: Tactics for Long Interviews
summary: Cara reviews a 3-hour interview she conducted with 14-year-old Isabel. Following an altercation between Isabel's mother and her stepfather's family, Isabel disclosed that her stepfather had been sexually abusing her when her mother wasn't home. Isabel was incredibly talkative, and her first narrative lasted over 30 minutes.

title: Consolidating Information Body Cam Interviews of Mother, Child, and Suspect
summary: The team examines a case handled by another CAC, reviewing a 6-year-old child's (RR) forensic interview along with body cam footage from the police interviews of the child, the mother, and the alleged abuser. RR alleged that her mother's boyfriend was touching her inappropriately on multiple occasions.

title: Minimization and Miscommunication
summary: Jordan interviews 8-year-old Alondra, who alleged repeated abuse by her two older brothers, Isaac (14) and Josue (16).

title: "Why is there a lotta . . . bad stuff happening in our house?" Bodycams on Esther (6), Ana (9), and Bryan (11)
summary: Part 3 of a series in which Jordan interviewed three siblings who alleged abuse from the same perpetrator. After previously reviewing Ana (9) and Esther's (6) forensic interviews for developmental differences in recollection, the team examines Bryan's (11) forensic interview to discuss delayed disclosure and reluctance.

title: Reluctance or Recall?
summary: Continuing the discussion of Jordan's interviews with three siblings who alleged abuse from the same perpetrator. The team looks at the older two siblings' interviews to discuss developmental differences in the recollection and narrative of the same event.

title: Interviewing by Age
summary: The team begins a discussion of a case in which Jordan interviewed three siblings who alleged abuse from the same perpetrator, starting with the interviews of the younger two siblings (Ana, 9, and Esther, 6) who both disclosed joint abuse. Ana reported to a teacher that her adult brother Augustin tried to put his penis in her and her sister's mouth.

title: Minimal Facts Interviewing: Expert Panel Discussion
summary: The team is joined by an expert panel to discuss the pros and cons of minimal facts interviews by first responders — what they are, when they are warranted (and when immediate CAC referral is preferable), what factors to consider, and what good questions look like.

title: Body Cam vs Forensic Interview
summary: The team discusses a 13-year-old child's disclosure of repeated abuse by her stepfather, starting with examination of the body cam footage of the first responders. The discussion covers how minimal facts interviewing could improve the investigative process and reduce inconsistencies, and steps forensic interviewers might take to address those inconsistencies.

title: Clarifying Sexual Touch (Part 2)
summary: Building on Part 1, the team reviews effective strategies for eliciting details regarding sexual touch and penetration. The webinar presents examples of questioning that went well and not so well, including the use of diagrams, tissue boxes, and very direct questions, and discusses ideas for working with extremely reluctant children when all other strategies fail.

title: Clarifying Sexual Touch (Part 1)
summary: The team reviews effective strategies for eliciting details regarding sexual touch and penetration, covering the legal standards, limited research on how best to ask questions, and examples of questioning that went well and not so well. The discussion includes the 'tissue box test' as a possible approach.

title: "Cocomelon says that" Danely (5)
summary: Jordan interviews 5-year-old Danely, who disclosed abuse by her older brother Ethan, who has autism. Danely reported that Ethan asked her and her cousin to play hospital and take off their pants, then touched the girls in their privates. Danely was very energetic and distractible, and the team reviews effective strategies for young children who are chatty but reluctant.

title: Araceli (13): What do you mean?
summary: The team is joined by special guest and fellow forensic interviewer Crystal Thorne. They peer-review an interview Crystal conducted with a shy and reluctant 12-year-old girl who disclosed sexual abuse by her paternal grandfather. The discussion covers Crystal's methods, tactics for overcoming reluctance, and the NICHD recommended supportive statements.

title: "I'm pretty sure you know what that is" AJ (13)
summary: Cara interviews 13-year-old AJ, a trans boy with he/him pronouns who is severely suicidal. AJ gave a note to his adult sister disclosing long-term repeated rape and sodomy by their stepfather, and the sister then filed a police report. The team reflects on a previous interview Tom conducted with a trans boy and compares the two cases, discussing risk factors trans youth face and how to incorporate suicide assessments into practice.

title: Peer Review Recommendations (Lisbet, 10)
summary: The team debuts their Peer Review Template in Google Sheets, teaching viewers how to access the template along with tips and tricks for using it. The webinar walks through the peer-review process including Question Type coding, using an interview conducted at the center in 2007.

title: "It was really tight that my hand couldn't breathe" Desiree (10)
summary: Jordan interviews 10-year-old Desiree. Spurred by an allegation of inappropriate touch from a maternal aunt, Desiree's mother asked her two daughters if stepfather Alberto had been touching them inappropriately. Desiree confirmed that Alberto had touched her inappropriately and later reported sodomy and vaginal touch to law enforcement and social workers. The team examines Jordan's interviewing strategies, the most effective language used, and tactics that helped Desiree overcome her reluctance.

title: "I get mad at my brain and sometimes I hate it" Lorenzo (7)
summary: Jordan interviews 7-year-old Lorenzo regarding two perpetrators — his stepfather and a friend his age. Lorenzo first reported sexual abuse by his stepfather when he was 4 years old, and DCFS found the count was sustained. In 2022, DCFS was informed that Lorenzo now states the perpetrator was not the stepfather, but a friend his own age. The team discusses the case, both interviews, and the challenges of interviewing young children.

title: "Right here it will be black all the time" Ellie (13)
summary: The team returns to basics by focusing on the structure and assets of the 10-Step, looking at Cara's December 2022 interview with 13-year-old Ellie. Ellie disclosed being touched by her father repeatedly over a 2-month period. Ellie was pretty reluctant, so the team examines which supportive statements helped her overcome reluctance and discusses strategies Cara could have used to elicit more detailed responses.

title: "Right here it will be black all the time" Chantal (12)
summary: The team reviews Catherine Liang's 2016 interview with 12-year-old Chantal, who had previously reported severe sexual abuse from her father. During the interview, Chantal partially recanted and greatly minimized the abuse. The team analyzes Catherine's approach for a partial recantation, discussing her successes and areas for improvement.

title: Alondra (5): Is it Abuse? "Because he never brings all my Barbies"
summary: An interview with 5-year-old Alondra, who disclosed that her father touched her private part while bathing her during a custody visit. The case raises difficult questions about distinguishing routine caretaking from sexual abuse, particularly given Alondra's age, her father's unfamiliarity with bathing her, and her history of vulvovaginitis. The discussion explores how question type affects information quality from young children, the challenges of interpreting ambiguous disclosures, and how prior allegations within the same family can both increase suspicion and complicate interpretation.

title: Justin (9): I haven't really been feeling like myself
summary: Cara interviews 9-year-old Justin, who was abused by his father. The team discusses Justin's reluctance and resistance to allegation questions, and the ways the 10-Step helped Justin overcome his reluctance and eventually disclose new information, including a second incident of abuse. The discussion also covers tactics for reducing a child's anxiety and emotional arousal.

title: Dayana (8) What percent are you in? If you get to 100, are you done?
summary: Continuing their discussion of assent with child psychologist and forensic interviewer Lauren Maltby, the team takes a closer look at Jordan's two interviews with 8-year-old Dayana. Dayana was extremely reluctant and had an intense emotional reaction to disclosure questions. The team examines how Jordan used assent to negotiate Dayana's return for a second interview and eventual disclosure, and how the 10-Step helped Dayana overcome her extreme reluctance.

title: Are children capable of informed consent?
summary: Special guest Lauren Maltby (child psychologist and forensic interviewer at Harbor UCLA) joins to discuss the process of obtaining assent from a child before an interview. Using the transcript of an assent conversation Lauren had with a teen, the team analyzes how an interviewer can obtain assent and discusses the benefits and concerns of incorporating assent into common practice. The team also looks at an interview Jordan conducted with an extremely reluctant child and examines how obtaining assent helped Jordan negotiate disclosure.

title: Emely (11) Revisited: I just wanted to creep into a little ball
summary: The team reviews their first ever webinar — 11-year-old Emely's interview — and examines the ways the 10-Step has changed over the years both formally and informally. The review highlights the work of a previous interviewer, Chrissy Del Pozzo, and changes in interviewing practices over the last 5 years.

title: "And I was like, yes I know what my body parts are." Clay (12)
summary: The team discusses Cara's first interview, a case with a 12-year-old trans boy. The webinar reviews successes, areas for improvement, and interviewing strategies. The team also discusses the child's discussion of his previous disclosures and risk factors for reluctance, and analyzes the general interviewing strategy according to the 10-Step and the importance of each tactic.

title: Mikayla (14)
summary: Jordan interviews 14-year-old Mikayla, who had been kidnapped and then sexually abused along with her friend. The team reviews the interview and discusses the inconsistencies of the minor's disclosures to law enforcement and children's services. Topics include how the perceived inconsistencies affected the case, how to ask about inconsistencies in a supportive manner, and how to question teenagers about sensitive topics without implying they are at fault.

title: Dylan (13)
summary: Dylan (13) was interviewed by Owen based on allegations of abuse made by his sister, despite never having disclosed himself. Dr. Lyon and team discuss preparing for an interview with limited information, overcoming reluctance to disclose, and providing neutral support during a forensic interview. The team reviews the supportive statements suggested in the Revised NICHD Protocol and shares some supportive techniques they often use.

title: "How much little girls and young women know about their genitalia, and how little the law understands"
summary: The USC Center for the Changing Family and the Child Interviewing Lab hosted a virtual panel event on the difficulties in questioning girls and young women about their genitalia in cases of sexual abuse and rape. Dr. Thomas Lyon discussed the legal requirements for establishing the nature and invasiveness of genital touch. Dr. Shalon Nienow described the process of forensic pediatric genital examinations and her experience assessing children's and adolescents' knowledge of genital anatomy. Dr. Zsofia Szojka concluded by presenting preliminary findings revealing difficulties in attorneys' questioning of children in sexual abuse and rape trials.

title: Force
summary: Dr. Lyon, Jordan, and Owen discuss establishing the use of force in child abuse cases. The webinar covers the legal requirements for force and legal cases describing what is sufficient, examines how children describe force and resistance, and discusses the dangers in asking children yes/no questions about force and resistance.

title: "I could just imagine the pain my mom is going through" Jacqueline R. (10)
summary: Jordan Sargent's 2018 interview with 10-year-old Jacqueline is reviewed four years later, with suggestions for improvement. Issues discussed include script vs. episodic recall, the 'pseudotemporal' problem, and providing support while remaining objective. The team also discusses strategies for peer reviewing past interviews and continuously improving as an interviewer.

title: 4- to 15-year-olds' difficulties in interpreting invitations asking "about the time"
summary: Dr. Lyon and staff present several research projects from the lab: (1) Owen Friend explores children's difficulties interpreting temporal invitations in forensic interviews, with suggestions for asking about specific 'times' (first, last, worst, etc.); (2) Hannah Siepmann examines how adolescent victims of commercial sexual exploitation are perceived by juries when they exhibit reluctance in court, and whether race affects this perception; (3) Dr. Zsofia Szojka investigates children's sensitivity to implied Wh- questions in yes/no questions with 'some' and 'any'; (4) Aga Nogalska examines how adolescent victims express reluctance during forensic interviews and how prior disclosure influences reluctance.

title: Truth-Lie Competency (& the Ten Step)
summary: Dr. Lyon and team discuss issues regarding children's competency to testify, including literature on children's understanding of truth and lies, legal requirements for children to be deemed competent to testify, and when/how to conduct a competency assessment. The team also discusses the interviewing protocol used for training in Washington state and compares Washington's protocols to the Ten Step 3.0.

title: "And she was just laughing and telling me basically, you're high it's not true." 14-year-old Lenay (Part 2)
summary: A follow-up to the previous case review: 14-year-old Lenay recanted sexual abuse allegations she had made against her stepfather, but had her original allegation to police captured via body-worn camera. Dr. Lyon and Jordan discuss issues regarding police interviews recorded on body-worn cameras and the pros and cons of recording interviews with child victims.

title: "And she was just laughing and telling me basically, you're high it's not true." 14-year-old Lenay
summary: Owen Friend interviews 14-year-old Lenay, who recanted sexual abuse allegations she had made against her stepfather. Dr. Lyon and Owen discuss preparing for an interview when expecting a recantation, supportive strategies for reluctant children, and issues regarding police interviews recorded on body-worn cameras.

title: "Are we done yet? Are we almost done? Are we done yet? [Yodels into juice box]" 7-year old Nala
summary: Jordan Sargent's interview with 7-year-old Nala is reviewed three years after it was conducted, with suggestions for improvement. Issues discussed include maintaining the attention of a distracted child, using support to overcome reluctance, and distinguishing between episodic and script recall.

title: "Sometimes I kinda wish that I didn't say anything at all" 14-year-old Sayuri
summary: Jordan Sargent interviews 14-year-old Sayuri (referred to as 'S' in the description). The team discusses repeated interviews for children who are initially unwilling to disclose, including improvised interview structure for particularly reluctant children, supportive strategies, script vs. episodic invitations, and ambivalence towards promising to tell the truth.

title: Recommendations for improving recantation interviews Sofia (12), Isabella (13) and Emma (10) "it's the truth that I'm lying"
summary: Dr. Lyon and team review recantations from other Child Advocacy Centers and provide peer review, discussing interview protocol for children who recant. Issues include how to structure a recant interview, how to ask children about prior disclosures, and how to provide support for recanters.

title: 11-year-old Valerie: but my dad never touched me in my life, never ever ever ever ever ever ever ever ever ever ever ever ever ever never
summary: Owen Friend interviews 11-year-old Valerie. The team discusses dealing with spontaneous disclosure during rapport building, regaining a child who has lost focus, providing support and clarification for reluctant children, and differences in screening for sexual and physical abuse.

title: 6-year-old Brittany: "Kids can't really know this"
summary: Jordan Sargent interviews 6-year-old Brittany. The team discusses how to implement the 10-Step with younger children, issues with interviewing younger children remotely, and how to use NEXT and MORE invitations to elicit a complete narrative.

title: The (Annotated) Ten Step Interview (Version 3)
summary: Dr. Tom Lyon and team continue discussing updates and changes to the 10-Step forensic interviewing protocol, taking a detailed look at the annotated version of the protocol.

title: The Ten Step Investigative Interview (Version 3)
summary: Dr. Tom Lyon and team discuss updates and changes to the 10-Step forensic interviewing protocol.

title: Productive Wh- Questions: Felt, Seen, Heard, Said, Hands and Mouth
summary: The team discusses supplemental Wh- questions that they have found to be especially effective, including references to what was seen, heard, said, and done with the hands and mouth. The webinar gives examples from their interviews and discusses why these questions may elicit information that invitations do not, including both experimental and field studies that examine their effectiveness.

title: 12-year-old Andrea: "I ruined everything and I just want everything to go back to normal"
summary: Jordan Sargent interviews 12-year-old Andrea, who recanted her allegations. The team reviews different techniques to use in order to still have a productive interview, covers common risk factors that increase the likelihood of recantation, and shares statistics from their sample of recanters collected over the years.

title: Note-Taking During Forensic Interviews
summary: Georgia Lundon discusses the research surrounding the perceived risks and benefits of note-taking, and suggests that the benefits far outweigh the potential costs. This webinar features a practice element and a Q&A from attendees. PowerPoint slides with links to mentioned research are available in a shared Google Drive folder.

title: "It was like if someone put like a big food in my mouth and I couldn't fit it." (7-year-old Christopher)
summary: Jordan Sargent interviews 7-year-old Christopher. The team discusses how to overcome young grade school children's difficulties in providing a narrative through Wh- questions that enable them to proceed step by step.

title: "But then I heard the story, what happened to Serenity" (8-year-old Savannah)
summary: Following on from the previous webinar on Serenity and Savannah, the team discusses how 8-year-old Savannah was eager to help her sister's story, and how her eagerness could be challenged by the defense later on. The team discusses the best way to encourage children to report on what they saw, rather than what they have heard from others.

title: "And in my child mind I didn't know anything that it was bad" (13-year-old Serenity & 8-year-old Savannah)
summary: Jordan Sargent interviews 13-year-old Serenity and 8-year-old Savannah. The team discusses how bribes might have caused one sister to be more reluctant to disclose abuse and experience feelings of self-blame, and how some 'milder' forms of abuse may be more traumatic for some children.

title: "My mom is going to choose him over all of us" (14-year-old Tiara & 10-year-old Scarlet) (Part 2)
summary: Jordan Sargent interviews sisters 14-year-old Tiara and 10-year-old Scarlet. The team discusses the early stages of abuse and the different reactions of both girls, as well as sibling dynamics and supportiveness, corroboration, recantation, maternal supportiveness, familial pressures, and the impact of disclosure on mental health.

title: "My mom is going to choose him over all of us" (14-year-old Tiara & 10-year-old Scarlet)
summary: Technical issues occurred early in this webinar, but the team hosted a Q&A session with many interesting questions from attendees.

title: Esperanza (14 years old)
summary: Hailey Konovalov interviews 14-year-old Esperanza, who immediately disclosed the abuse. The team discusses why and how this may have occurred and compares it to delayed disclosures. The interview addresses abuse dynamics and how the trauma of the abuse impacts the child, with discussion particularly helpful for interviewers struggling with how to follow up on a long and productive initial narrative.

title: Recantation: Azul (13)
summary: This webinar focuses on 13-year-old Azul, who disclosed abuse to friends through social media before later recanting. The discussion highlights best practices for interviewing youth who have made multiple disclosures, documenting prior reports, and understanding how family reactions may influence a child's willingness to maintain or withdraw allegations.

title: Question Type and Productivity: Bryanna (13)
summary: This training-focused webinar examines forensic interviewing methods and the relationship between question types and the amount of information children provide. Using a real interview as an example, the presenters analyze open-ended questioning, narrative development, and techniques that encourage detailed and reliable responses.

title: Question Type and Productivity: Delilah (11) and Bryanna (13)
summary: This webinar explores how different interviewing approaches affect the quantity and quality of information obtained from children. Through case examples, the presenters discuss the impact of open-ended prompts, potential investigator bias, and strategies for obtaining detailed narratives while maintaining a neutral interviewing stance.

title: Case Review: 14 year old Deavyn
summary: This webinar examines one of the lab's early remote forensic interviews and discusses the benefits and challenges of conducting child interviews through video technology. The presenters review interviewing techniques, rapport building in virtual settings, and considerations for maintaining interview quality when in-person interviews are not possible.

title: Case Review: 12 year old Lesly
summary: This webinar reviews a case involving repeated allegations of abuse and explores how caregiver responses can influence disclosure patterns. The discussion focuses on family support, disbelief, blame, and the role these factors play in children's willingness to maintain or withdraw allegations over time.

title: Case Review: 13 year old Renee
summary: This webinar examines a case involving 13-year-old Renee, who later recanted previous allegations of sexual abuse. The discussion focuses on common reasons children recant, how family dynamics and concerns about disrupting relationships can influence disclosures, and effective interviewing strategies for exploring prior statements without pressuring the child. Viewers learn how forensic interviewers evaluate competing explanations for disclosure and recantation.

title: Case Review: 11 year old Matthew
summary: This webinar examines a case involving 11-year-old Matthew, who disclosed repeated sexual abuse. The presenters discuss unique challenges that may arise when interviewing male victims, including embarrassment, shame, reluctance to discuss abuse, and strategies for helping children provide detailed narratives in a supportive environment.

title: Case Review: 9 year old Faith
summary: This webinar reviews a case involving allegations of problematic sexual behavior between siblings and explores the challenges of interviewing children when caregivers disagree about what occurred. The presenters discuss credibility assessment, family responses to disclosures, and factors that may increase the likelihood of recantation or inconsistent reporting.
